Dilip Patra & Ors vs State Nct Of Delhi & Anr on 17 February,
2023

Author: Swarana Kanta Sharma
Bench: Swarana Kanta Sharma

 petitioners.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
versus
 State Nct Of Delhi & Anr. ..

Through: Mr. Naresh Kumar Chah
 the State with Io.

Mr. A. Nayal, Advocat  CORAM:
 HON'BLE MS. JUSTICE SWARANA KANTA SHARMA  ORDER % 17.02.2023 CRL.M.A. 4313/2023 (exemption)
1. Allowed, subject to all just exceptions.
2. Application stands disposed of.

3. The instant petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973("Cr.P.C.") has been filed by the petitioners seeking quashing of FIR bearing no. 594/2019 registered at Police Station Mehrauli, Delhi for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 ("IPC") and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom.
4. Issue notice.
Mr. Naresh Kumar Chahar, learned APP accepts notice on behalf of the State.
5. Petitioners are present before this Court and have been identified by their counsel Mr. Hamid Hawari and Investigating Officer (IO) from Police Station Mehrauli, Delhi.
6. Brief facts of the present case are that petitioner no. 1 married to respondent no. 2 on 12.02.2009 according to Hindu Vedic Rites and Ceremonies.
It is stated that differences between petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2 has arisen in few months and the parties are living separately from each other 22.08.2018.
On the complaint of respondent no.2, an FIR bearing no. 594/2019 was registered at Police Station Mehrauli, for the offences punishable under Section 498A/406/34 of IPC.

It is further stated that the parties have resolved their differences before Mediation Centre, Saket courts, New Dilip Patra & Ors vs State Nct Of Delhi & Anr on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18871968/
1 Delhi on 08.12.2020.

entities.text: New Dilip Patra & Ors vs State Nct Of Delhi & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7. On a query made by this Court, respondent no. 2 who has been identified by the IO, has categorically stated that she has entered into compromise out of her own free will and without any pressure, coercion or threat.
It is also stated by respondent no. 2 that the entire dispute has been amicably settled between the parties before Mediaton Centre, Saket Courts, New Delhi on 08.12.2020.

entities.text: Mediaton Centre, Saket Courts, New Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
8. It is submitted that respondent no. 2 has settled all her claims in respect of her dowry articles,
stridhan, marriage expenses, jewellery, gift items and claims of past, present and future maintenance and permanent alimony with petitioners.

9. The petitioner no. 1 had paid a sum of Rs. 6,25,000/- in three installments in the following manner:
a. First installment of Rs.2,25,000/- paid to respondent no. 2 at the time of recording of statements of first motion;
b. Second installment of Rs. 2,00,000/- paid to respondent no. 2 at the time of recording of statement of second motion; c. Third/Final instalment of Rs. 2,00,000/-
to be paid at the time of quashing of the FIR before the Honble High Court at New Delhi.

10. Today, the complainant who is present in Court states that she has received the last and final instalment of Rs. 2,00,000/- today, i.e., 17.02.2023 by way of Demand Draft bearing no. 026035 drawn on HDFC Bank, Gurgaon, and has no objection if the FIR in question is quashed.

11. In view of the above facts that the parties have amicably resolved their differences out of their own free will, and without any coercion, no useful purpose will be served by continuing the proceedings, rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
It would thus be in interest of justice to quash the abovementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
There is no legal impediment in quashing the FIR in question.

12. Accordingly, FIR bearing no. 594/2019 registered at Police Station Mehrauli, Delhi for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of IPC and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
13. In view of above, the present petition stands disposed of.
14. The order be uploaded on the website forthwith.
SWARANA KANTA SHARMA, J FEBRUARY 17, 2023/kss
